chapter: Billie Holiday and the band's singers
title: Helen Humes, Thelma Carpenter and the band's women singers
summary: Jones sorts out the sequence of women vocalists, from Billie to Helen Humes to Thelma Carpenter at the Lincoln Hotel's Blue Room.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: How long did Helen stay there?
Helen stayed with the band, as far as I know - '40, '41, '42 - something happened I think around about -
She stayed after you left, didn't she?
No, she did not. We got Thelma Carpenter.
Thelma came in there for a spell.
But she evidently came back, didn't she?

Helen never came back. No, no, she never came back with a small group because Helen went out on her own. She didn't need any one, you know, because you remember in show business you started early and Helen started early. We had Thelma to come in but something happened with Thelma and then we sent Thelma out for a minute and then we brought Thelma back when we went into Marie Kramer's hotel.
Hotel Edison, that's right. No, not the Edison - Lincoln.
The Blue Room. That was on Eighth Avenue.

Hotel had the beautiful Blue Room. She had 11 hotels. Thelma Carpenter was our vocalist. We didn't have nobody but Jimmie Rushing; and the only women vocalists that sang in that band at that time was from Billie to Helen Humes to Thelma, and then Thelma was out. We didn't have no other woman.
